- When sentiment is negative or near-zero, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30-day horizon.
- After a recent price spike, model often overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of downward trend), model tends to ignore it; adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day moving average.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.2), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% for 30-day horizon.
- Model consistently underestimates in low-sentiment periods with strong downward momentum; add 2–5% buffer if sentiment < 0.1 and price has fallen >5% in last 5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model’s first 5 days are significantly below true outcome, apply a “lag correction” — shift forecast up by 0.5–1.5% per day for the first 5 days to account for delayed reaction.
